To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Cortisol administration to adrenalectomised rats resulted in an increase in the activity of amino acid incorporating ability of liver ribosomes in vivo, and that light polysomes from cortisol-treated rats exhibited a higher activity in vitro than those obtained from adrenaletcomised rats.

1) the activity of amino acid incorporating activity of purified ribosomes obtained from cortisol-treated animals is significantly higher than that of ribosomes from control animals, and 2) the activity of light polysomes obtained after fractionation of polysomal preparations from cortisol-treated rats was twice as high as that from control animals.

cortisol treatment increases the activity of poly U-dependent amino acid incorporation in vitro by ribosomal and light polysomal preparations from the liver of adrenalectomised rats, and the increase is retained after removal of endogenous m RNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of adrenalectomy and corticosterone administration on the activity of poly U directed amino acid incorporation by rat liver ribosome and polysomes in vitro.
the effect of the adrenal hormone, cortisol, on the activity of amino acid incorporating systems in rat liver.
a possible mechanism of action of the steroid hormone cortisol on the activity of amino acid incorporating system of rat liver ribosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cortisol treatment in vivo increased amino acid incorporation by ribosomes in vitro, but the increase was not observed in the case of heavy polysomes.
in the liver of adrenalectomised rats, the incorporation of amino acids into protein in vitro is depressed.
the activity of protein biosynthesis is enhanced in rat liver by cortisol treatment in vivo, but the mechanism is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the administration of cortisol in vivo increases the activity of protein-synthesis in rat liver, which is due to the increased activity of ribosomes and light polysomes.

the activity of protein-synthesis by ribosomal and polysome preparations is enhanced by administration of cortisol in vivo, and that the enhancement of the activity of protein syntheses by polysome fractions is due to the increase in the activity of the light polysome fractions.
cortisol treatment in vivo increases the activity of protein biosynthesis at the level of ribosomes, but not at that of polysomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

cortisol-treatment increases the rate of protein synthesis by light polysomes, but not by the heavy polysomes, and that the increase in the activity is not due to the increase in the number of ribosomes per polysomes.

cortisol administration in vivo increases the activity of poly U directed amino acid incorporation in vitro by ribosomal fraction and light polysomes, and that this effect is not due to an increase in m-RNA activity.
cortisol administration in vivo increases the activity of protein biosynthesis by rat liver ribosome in vitro.
